rounds.text: Homre Ltd demonstrates exceptional fundamental momentum, highlighted by a staggering 314% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months and a 102% surge over three years [E16, E17]. This acceleration is underpinned by robust operational efficiency, generating an impressive ROCE of 37.65% that comfortably outpaces the sector benchmark of 12.5% [E10]. The balance sheet is pristine, featuring zero debt down from Rs 0.11 Cr, supported by solid financial health where operating cash flow fully matched operating profit at 100% in March 2026 [E32, E34, E55]. Valuation metrics present an attractive entry point, as a discounted cash flow model establishes an intrinsic value of Rs 3 per share against the current market price of Rs 2.17, delivering a tangible 28.9% margin of safety [E40, E41]. Furthermore, the company operates within a supportive Consumer Durables macro backdrop benefiting from a sector tailwind score of 0.75 and outperforming the sector median profit growth of 16.0% [E67, E68]. Conceded: the company carries a low median return on equity of 3% over the last 3 years and an inconsistent operating margin trend [E24, E28, E58].

Despite recent profit surges, Homre Ltd carries severe valuation disconnects and underlying fundamental vulnerabilities. The stock trades at an extreme P/E of 217x against a sector benchmark of 41.58x and a staggering P/B of 150.11x compared to the sector benchmark of 7.05x [E6, E7]. Long-term profitability metrics expose chronic weakness, highlighted by a 10-year median return on equity of -1%, a 5-year median ROE of 1%, and a low 3-year average ROE of just 2.71% [E22, E23, E58]. Operating margins remain thin at 5% in the trailing twelve months with inconsistent yearly and quarterly trends [E26, E27, E28], while reported earnings are contaminated by Rs 0.62 Cr in other income [E59]. Furthermore, the company exhibits extreme historical risk with an annualized volatility of 88.4% and a devastating worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -99.6% [E48, E49]. Insider confidence is waning as promoter holdings have dropped by 2.63 percentage points overall and continue to slide quarter-over-quarter [E36, E57]. Conceded: the company carries zero debt, has boosted operating cash flows, and features a strong 3-year compounded profit growth of 102% alongside a high ROCE [E16, E33, E34, E65].

Conceded: [E6], [E7], [E22], [E23], [E48], [E49], [E57], and [E59]. The bear's fixation on historical multi-year ROE medians ignores the pivotal inflection point where the company's median return on equity has already surged to 11% [E25] and ROCE stands at an impressive 37.65% against a sector benchmark of 12.5% [E10]. While operating margins sit at 5% [E26], compounding profit growth has accelerated dramatically to 102% over 3 years and 314% over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17], proving that recent momentum easily overrides legacy volatility. The concerns regarding insider holdings overlook the fact that promoters still retain a commanding 64.99% majority stake [E36], anchoring management alignment directly with shareholders. Furthermore, the supposed valuation disconnect is fully neutralized by a reverse DCF showing the market price only requires 13.4% earnings growth—comfortably below the 18.0% base case assumption [E42]—while the rules-based engine scores the setup at a solid 86 out of 100 [E60].

Conceded: [E10] and [E42]. The bull’s reliance on recent surging profitability ignores the company's dismal long-term operational record, characterized by a 10-year median ROE of -1% [E22], a 5-year median ROE of just 1% [E23], and a 3-year median ROE of 3% [E24]. Furthermore, earnings are artificially padded by non-core inflows, as profits explicitly include Rs. 0.62 Cr of other income [E59]. The bull's dismissal of insider selling is flawed because promoter holding has actively eroded from 67.62% to 64.99% [E36], with an additional drop noted over the last quarter [E57]. Finally, the claim of robust momentum is undermined by an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E27, E28] alongside a thin 5% operating margin in the trailing twelve months [E26].
